findings.title: English reference file lookup is fragile and may throw unhandled exceptions
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml` derives the English reference file path by naively doing `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. If a path contains "resources-community" multiple times, or the filename pattern doesn't match (e.g. en file itself, or a locale name containing unexpected characters), this can produce an incorrect path. More importantly, if the computed `englishFile` doesn't exist (e.g. missing en counterpart for a given theme/module), `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws FileNotFoundException, which is wrapped as an unchecked `RuntimeException` propagated out of `verify()`, which only declares `MojoExecutionException`. This will crash the whole build for any file without a matching English counterpart rather than reporting a soft validation failure.

findings.title: santizeAnchors uses replaceFirst on whole string potentially matching wrong occurrence
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` iterates anchor tags found via the matcher, but calls `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` against the *original* `value` string on each loop iteration, not the updated local variable's position context. If the same anchor tag string appears multiple times in `value`, repeated calls to `replaceFirst` with the same pattern will always remove the first occurrence, never advancing past already-processed matches, potentially stripping the wrong occurrence or looping incorrectly relative to `matcher`'s cursor (which continues scanning the original `value`, not the mutated one), causing find/replace to get out of sync and produce incorrect sanitized results or false positive 'anchor mismatch' messages.

findings.title: normalizeValue hardcodes key-specific exceptions reducing maintainability/generality
findings.body: normalizeValue special-cases specific keys ("templateHelp", "optimizeLookupHelp", keys starting with "linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit", or "error-invalid-multivalued-size") directly in the verifier logic instead of deriving these exceptions from data/config. Any new translation key introducing legitimate special syntax (e.g., new choice-format messages or generic placeholders resembling HTML tags) will trigger false-positive 'Illegal HTML' failures until the verifier code itself is updated, creating ongoing maintenance burden tied to translation content changes rather than to code changes.

findings.title: verify() swallows RuntimeExceptions raised deep in verifySafeHtml without proper MojoExecutionException wrapping
findings.body: `verify()` catches only `IOException` around `verifySafeHtml()`, but `verifySafeHtml()` internally throws unchecked `RuntimeException` (for FileNotFoundException-like issues) rather than IOException. These RuntimeExceptions will propagate uncaught out of `verify()`, breaking the stated `throws MojoExecutionException` contract and potentially causing an unhandled build failure with a less helpful stack trace instead of a clean MojoExecutionException.
